classification.difficultyReason: Construct a single-cut rearrangement and generalise its area argument to the difference of two squares.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The figure opposite represents a square piece of paper with a corner cut out. Make a single straight cut to reshape the paper to form a rectangle with length $a+2$ and width $a-2$. This illustrates $a^2-4=(a+2)(a-2)$.

spec.description: Unshaded square with its bottom-right square corner removed; top and left sides labelled a, both notch edges labelled 2. Coordinates are schematic.
spec.mathematics: Square side a with a 2 by 2 square removed from the bottom-right corner.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied outline and four givens are visible.

answer.short: Cut from the top-left corner to the inner corner of the notch. Rotate the lower-left piece through $90^\circ$ anticlockwise and join the sloping edges to form an $(a+2)$ by $(a-2)$ rectangle.
answer.worked:
Cut along the dashed line from the top-left corner to the inner corner of the notch. Rotate the lower-left trapezium through $90^\circ$ anticlockwise, then translate the pieces to join their sloping edges as shown. The rectangle has length $a+2$ and width $a-2$. Since cutting and rearranging preserves area,

$$\begin{align*}a^2-2^2&=(a+2)(a-2)\\a^2-4&=(a+2)(a-2).\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Complete cut-and-rearrangement figure. The dashed cut joins the top-left corner to the inner notch corner. The resulting rectangle retains the teacher figure's segment labels and diagonal seam.
spec.mathematics: Two congruent trapeziums form a rectangle of dimensions a+2 and a-2.

answer.short: Remove a $b$ by $b$ corner from an $a$ by $a$ square. Cut from the opposite corner to the inner notch corner, then rearrange the pieces into an $(a+b)$ by $(a-b)$ rectangle.
answer.worked:
Use the same construction with the removed corner of side $b$. Cut from the top-left corner to the inner corner of the notch. Rotate the lower-left trapezium through $90^\circ$ anticlockwise, then translate the pieces to join their sloping edges. The resulting rectangle has length $a+b$ and width $a-b$. Its area equals the area of the original square minus the removed square:

$$a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b).$$
